question.knowledge_point: Finding the Acceleration Vector of a Particle Given Its Position Vector
question.problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨\frac{{t}^{5}}{5},\,3{t}^{2}-1⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a.$
question.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{t}^{5}}{5}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨{t}^{4},\,6t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6t)⟩ \\  & =⟨4{t}^{3},\,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$
